what_happened: Scope gap in this task's own description, verified against the current source before filing, so a fix guided by it would be INCOMPLETE. This record's description says to fix 'BOTH call sites' (the --dry-run gate check at line 769 and the live gate check at line 901), but 'jq --argjson verdicts "$AUDIT_VERDICT_JSON"' appears at THREE sites. The unnamed third is line 934: the durable-evidence recording write that stamps audit_verdict/audit_override onto each new active_projects entry. Site 934 is materially different from the other two because it sits on the SUCCESS path rather than being a gate check -- it runs whenever the gate PASSES, so it is unavoidable even on a clean write and cannot be dodged by satisfying the gate. It falls under this record's general 'sweep for other internal jq invocations' clause but is not enumerated, and the explicit 'BOTH' framing actively points an implementer away from it. Additional diagnostic-quality wrinkle at that site, confirmed by reading it: its jq invocation ends '> "$AUDIT_RECORD_TMP" 2>/dev/null', so an E2BIG there is swallowed and surfaces only as the generic 'audit-evidence gate: failed to record audit evidence into the staged result' with exit 3, discarding the real cause -- a different and more misleading symptom than the bare 'Argument list too long' the other two sites produce. Second, smaller gap: this record quotes the spill mechanism's design claim as evidence but does not require correcting it. That claim lives verbatim at line 258 -- 'EFFECTIVE_FILTER prefix built below -- no existing or future --argjson call site has to change.' -- and is falsified by all three sites above, so the fix should correct or remove it rather than leaving a comment that will mislead the next reader. Context worth noting, deliberately NOT part of this task's scope: durable audit_verdict evidence cost 12-35KB per entry and grew specs/state.json by 114KB for three tasks (1.62MB to 1.73MB) in one conclusion stage, so verdict size scales with backlog size and this failure class will recur and worsen; whether to BOUND audit_verdict size is a separate question no backlog record currently covers. Corroboration that the defect is real and recurring: a conclusion stage in this session produced a 147KB verdict for 3 proposals against the ~110-record backlog and hard-stopped with 'Argument list too long' (exit 126), worked around by hand-collapsing to 63KB, dropping scope-blind and semantic-only-closed rulings while retaining every mechanically-corroborated and open-side ruling. 147KB is only ~1.5x the 100KB SPILL_THRESHOLD, so the existing spill machinery would have handled it correctly had the binding gone through the spill path -- this is a wiring gap, not a missing capability.
